note: Deny-list for scripts/ci/personal_data_scan.py.
This repo is PUBLIC and meant to be cloneable. It must contain zero real
personal or customer information. Every hash below stands for something
that was actually found in this tree during the 2026-08 scrub — a real
colleague or organiser name, a real customer, the author's employer, or
the author's personal email/username — or for a name a reviewer asked to
be blocked pre-emptively.
WHY HASHES AND NOT THE WORDS: a plain-text roster of colleagues' names
sitting in scripts/ci/ would put back exactly what the scrub removed. So
only sha256(salt | normalized term)[:16] is stored. This is OBFUSCATION,
NOT SECRECY — the salt is right here and a surname dictionary confirms a
guess. What it buys: the repo no longer states who these people are, so
no grep, scraper or casual reader recovers the list, while CI keeps exact
matching. Do not describe it as encryption.
HOW TO ADD A TERM
python scripts/ci/personal_data_scan.py add-term "Some Person"
python scripts/ci/personal_data_scan.py --report /tmp/pd.json
Confirm the second command still reports 0 findings, then commit this
file — WITHOUT naming the term in the commit message or PR description,
which are just as public as the tree.
python scripts/ci/personal_data_scan.py test-term "Some Person"
answers 'is this already blocked?' without adding anything.
WHAT DOES NOT BELONG HERE: common English words, bare common first names
('Mark', 'Ken', 'Dan'), and anything that identifies nobody on its own.
Matching is case-insensitive and punctuation-insensitive over 1-3 word
windows, so an over-broad term fires on ordinary prose — and a noisy
check is a check people learn to ignore. Three scrubbed customer names
are ordinary English words or common three-letter acronyms and were
deliberately left OUT for that reason; they were still renamed
everywhere in the tree, this list just cannot police them.
Normalization: casefold, then split on non-alphanumerics. So one hash
covers 'Rodriguez, Joshua' / 'rodriguez joshua', and 'firstname.lastname'
matches the spaced form of the same name.
Real people (colleagues, organisers, customer contacts) and real
organizations (customers, prospects, the author's employer and its
mail domain). Categories are not stored per hash on purpose: a
category label plus a hash narrows a brute-force guess.
Regex classes. These carry no identity of their own, so they stay in
plain text. `allow_captures` lists capture-group-1 values that are
accepted placeholders rather than a real identity.

Email address outside the reserved example/test domains

note: Deliberate, load-bearing exceptions. These are NOT personal-data leaks:
they are the published identity of the application itself, which cannot
change without breaking installed copies.
* github.com/<owner>/... — the repo's own public URL.
* the reverse-DNS bundle identifier / Android application id. Changing
either invalidates existing installs, their macOS TCC grants and
their update path.
* src-tauri publisher / copyright / authors — the app's legal
attribution. Replacing a real author with a fictional one would be a
false statement of authorship, not a privacy improvement.
The two `line_substrings` below are the literal owner-derived tokens in
those URLs and identifiers. They are already public by construction —
the clone URL contains them.
